subject: pass values in different functions in server.R

messages.author: 4e6060fd7b80ee80
messages.subject: pass values in different functions in server.R
parts:
Hey guys,

In my case, I fitted a classification tree, sth like "model<-repart(many arguments)", then my plot and model summary both requires the information in "model", my question is, instead of fitting the tree model twice in renderPlot and renderPrint, is there a way that I only fit the model once then we can use 'model' in both functions. Currently, my codes looks like following:



shinyServer(function(input, output){
 


 
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
  
    model<-rpart(form,method='class',
                 rpart.control(minsplit = input$minsplit),
                
                 parms=list(split=input$split))
   
   fancyRpartPlot(model)
   
 
  })

output$summary <- renderPrint({
    model<-rpart(form,method='class',
                 rpart.control(minsplit = input$minspli),
                
                 parms=list(split=input$split))
    summary(model)
  })
 

I tried to do sth like:

shinyServer(function(input, output){
 

  model<-reactive(rpart(form,method='class',
                 rpart.control(minsplit = input$minsplit),
                
                 parms=list(split=input$split)), 
                  env=parent.frame(),
                    quoted=FALSE,
                    label=NULL)
 
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
  
 
   
   fancyRpartPlot(model)
   
 
  })

output$summary <- renderPrint({
   
    summary(model)
  })
 

It seems this does not work....

Thank you,

Su

messages.author: 129e07bdb789652f
messages.subject: Re: pass values in different functions in server.R
parts:
Hi,

1) when I use model(), does Shiny fit the model again?

No, see my answer  here https://groups.google.com/d/topic/shiny-discuss/FlmsUs-7ckQ/discussion, and more explanations in the Shiny tutorial 

2) If I want to use model$control, neither model()$control nor model$work worked, any idea on how can I obtain the value of model$control in these functions of renderPlot and renderPrint?

You only have to be logic: use model()$control, not model$control, because model() is the output of your reactive conductor, not model.

Yours,
S
